# Shared-source gluing and an exact adaptive cap credit

This note treats TWO actual anchored barycentric relations with one shared source and one common target. It proves a joint directional credit which can strictly exceed the best fixed independent packing of those relations. The gain depends on actual target-event overlap. It can vanish identically, and no universal center or parity assembly is asserted.

## 1. Actual geometric and probabilistic data

Let K_z be the positive d-dimensional fibers of an actual convex mixed body, d>=1, over a finite integer base P. Put V_z=|K_z|. Fix distinct p,s in P and two nonempty disjoint source sets A,B, disjoint also from {p,s}, with positive barycentric coefficients such that

    p=lambda_s s+sum_(z in A)lambda_z z
     =nu_s s+sum_(z in B)nu_z z,
    lambda_s+sum_A lambda_z=nu_s+sum_B nu_z=1.       (1)

All coefficients in (1) are positive. Convex compatibility puts the corresponding Minkowski averages in K_p.

Let pi_1 be ANY coupling of the uniform probability laws on K_s and the K_z, z in A; let pi_2 similarly couple K_s with z in B. The two K_s marginals agree exactly. Disintegrate each coupling over the shared variable X_s and glue their conditional laws, initially independently. This gives one joint probability law Pi with BOTH original relation couplings as marginals. Every variable X_z remains uniform on its actual fiber, and

    Y_1=lambda_s X_s+sum_A lambda_z X_z in K_p,
    Y_2=nu_s X_s+sum_B nu_z X_z in K_p               (2)

almost surely. Their bases are both p. Existence of conditional laws is the standard compact-Euclidean disintegration statement already used in the archived boundary-coupling notes. Equivalently, bounded Borel conditional kernels give the glued law by integrating their product against the common uniform law on K_s.

The couplings may in particular be the actual multi-input triangular transports from `candidate 4bb4c167681e8955`. Then each target law has its proved Minkowski-volume density ceiling and its exact weighted centroid. Nothing in the argument replaces these laws by arbitrary densities or assumes their centroids equal g_(K_p). The new inequality itself needs only their actual marginals and the affine identities (2).

Fix THREE closed ambient halfspaces H_1,H_2,H_3. They may be oblique, vertical, or carry whole-fiber boundary mass. One and the same coupling Pi is used for all three. Set

    A_(r,i)={ (p,Y_r) in H_i }, r=1,2,
    f_(r,i)=Pr(A_(r,i)), o_i=Pr(A_(1,i) intersect A_(2,i)),
    U_(z,i)=|K_z intersect (H_i)_z|.

All events are Borel. Since a positive weighted average of strictly negative affine margins is strictly negative, (2) implies pointwise

    1_A(1,i) <= OR_(z in {s} union A) 1_{(z,X_z) in H_i},
    1_A(2,i) <= OR_(z in {s} union B) 1_{(z,X_z) in H_i}. (3)

The use of closed caps is exact: no boundary atom is deleted.

## 2. Exact shared-source credit

Put

    a=V_s, b=min_(z in A)V_z, c=min_(z in B)V_z,
    c1=min(a,b), c2=min(a,c), c12=min(a,b+c),
    rho=c1+c2-c12>=0.                              (4)

For each of the three caps, the captured volume in the DISTINCT source fibers obeys

    U_(s,i)+sum_A U_(z,i)+sum_B U_(z,i)
       >= c1 f_(1,i)+c2 f_(2,i)-rho o_i.           (5)

In particular the shared source is charged exactly once.

Proof. Give a captured source indicator at z the cost V_z. If only target event1 occurs, (3) forces cost at least c1. If only event2 occurs, it forces at least c2. If both occur, either the shared source is captured, at cost at least a, or at least one exclusive source from EACH relation is captured, at cost at least b+c. The minimum cost is c12. If neither occurs, use zero. Thus pointwise source cost is at least

    c1 1_A(1,i)+c2 1_A(2,i)-rho 1_A(1,i)1_A(2,i).

Its expectation on the left is exactly the left side of (5), since X_z is uniform on K_z. This proves (5).

For the information consisting only of the two Boolean implications (3), this is the optimal pointwise cost: each of the four target states is realized abstractly by its cheapest hitting set of source indicators. This sharpness claim is about Boolean incidence, not simultaneous convex realizability of arbitrary state tables.

## 3. Exact comparison with fixed independent packing

The strongest bound obtained by assigning two FIXED nonnegative coefficients to the separate target-event inequalities is

    L_i=max{theta_1 f_(1,i)+theta_2 f_(2,i):
        theta_1,theta_2>=0, theta_1<=b, theta_2<=c,
                                      theta_1+theta_2<=a}. (6)

The shared-source constraint is essential. The maximum is attained. If f_(1,i)>=f_(2,i), direct optimization gives

    L_i=c1 f_(1,i)+(c12-c1) f_(2,i).

Reverse the two labels in the other case. Consequently the new right side of (5) is EXACTLY

    L_i+rho[min(f_(1,i),f_(2,i))-o_i].             (7)

The bracket is nonnegative. It equals the smaller of the two directed crossing probabilities

    min{Pr(A_(1,i)\A_(2,i)), Pr(A_(2,i)\A_(1,i))}.

Thus the new inequality is strictly stronger than fixed independent packing precisely when rho>0 and both directed crossing events have positive probability. It is an adaptive hitting-set credit: the optimal assignment may depend on the two ACTUAL target states. It is not obtained by falsely summing two uses of the shared capacity.

This does NOT imply that (5) always dominates an unrelated stronger geometric inequality such as Brunn--Minkowski on residual bodies. Section6 gives an actual example in which those residual credits vanish while (7) is strictly stronger than (6). Conversely (7) can have zero gain, as Section7 shows.

## 4. Conditional support criteria; no incompatible per-cap optimizers

Let q_(r,i)(x)=Pr(A_(r,i)|X_s=x) for the two fixed relation couplings. Every gluing satisfies the conditional Frechet upper bound

    Pr(A_(1,i) intersect A_(2,i)|X_s=x)
                                      <=min(q_(1,i)(x),q_(2,i)(x)).

Writing expectations over the actual uniform X_s law, the gain bracket in (7) is therefore at least

    min{ E(q_(1,i)-q_(2,i))_+,
                         E(q_(2,i)-q_(1,i))_+ }.   (8)

Hence if the two conditional target probabilities cross on two positive-measure source subsets, positive gain is forced for EVERY gluing. This condition holds separately for any of the three caps, so all its conclusions hold simultaneously for one common coupling.

For the conditionally independent gluing, o_i=E[q_(1,i)q_(2,i)] exactly. Its gain is

    min{ E[q_(1,i)(1-q_(2,i))],
                         E[q_(2,i)(1-q_(1,i))] }. (9)

This is positive exactly when both displayed nonnegative integrals are positive. It may be positive even when (8) is zero. These are exact statements about actual conditional laws, not claims that a prescribed geometric family must satisfy them.

## 5. Retaining the full three-bit law under one optimized gluing

For each relation let Sigma_r=(1_A(r,1),1_A(r,2),1_A(r,3)) in {0,1}^3. Conditional on X_s=x, the two original couplings determine probabilities q_r(s|x), s in {0,1}^3. A joint conditional signature law is any 8 by8 nonnegative matrix T_(s,t)(x) with these row and column marginals.

For fixed weights omega_i>=0, a SINGLE coupling maximizing the weighted sum of the three right sides of (5) is obtained by minimizing

    sum_(s,t) T_(s,t)(x) sum_(i=1)^3 omega_i rho s_i t_i       (10)

at each x. The two marginal terms in (5) are fixed. A conditional optimizer can be chosen Borel. Indeed the finite transportation polytope is nonempty and compact. After deleting one redundant marginal equation, every vertex is given by one of finitely many independent column bases; its coordinates are linear functions of the Borel marginal entries. Feasibility of each candidate and comparison of their finite linear costs are Borel conditions. Choose the first feasible cost-minimizing candidate in a fixed ordering. Degenerate vertices and zero marginal entries cause no exception.

Now condition the original relation laws further on their own signatures. Given (x,s,t), sample their remaining input coordinates from those original conditional kernels, independently of each other. Integrate against the selected T(x) and the uniform X_s law. This reconstructs BOTH original relation laws exactly, realizes the chosen signature matrix, and keeps the affine target identities (2). Thus (10) is one realizable common gluing for the complete three-cap objective.

No assertion is made that it minimizes each o_i separately. Those three separate optima may be incompatible. The common finite objective (10), or the fixed independent gluing of Section4, avoids that quantifier error. The construction applies to any finite cap menu; three caps are retained explicitly here.

## 6. Actual rational rectangle chain with strict directional gain

Take n=1,d=2 and integer bases -1,0,1,2. For coordinates (x,y), prescribe centered rectangles

    K_-1=[-1,1] times[-1,1],
    K_0 =[-3,3] times[-1,1],
    K_1 =[-2,2] times[-1,1],
    K_2 =[-1,1] times[-1,1].                       (11)

These are the exact fibers of an ambient convex body: interpolate the x half-widths (1,3,2,1) affinely between consecutive bases. Their successive slopes are2,-1,-1, so the half-width function is concave; the y interval stays fixed. This gives a compact convex body with interior and precisely these four integer fibers.

The common target p=0 has relations

    0=(-1+1)/2=(2/3)(-1)+(1/3)2.                  (12)

Let (X,Y) be uniform on [-1,1]^2. Use X_s=(X,Y), X_1=(2X,Y), X_2=(X,Y). These are actual uniform source marginals and realize BOTH relation couplings. Their target points are

    Y_1=(3X/2,Y), Y_2=(X,Y),                     (13)

both in K_0. They retain their actual uniform rectangle laws, not merely density ceilings.

Choose the three ambient caps, all with zero base coefficient,

    H_1={x+y>=0}, H_2={-x+y>=0}, H_3={-y>=0}.      (14)

For H_1 and H_2, each target event has probability1/2, their intersection has probability11/24, and both directed differences have probability1/24. For example one H_1 difference has area

    integral_0^(2/3) x/2 dx+integral_(2/3)^1(1-x)dx=1/6

in the square of area4. Symmetry gives the other difference. For H_3 the events coincide exactly and the intersection probability is1/2.

Here a=4,b=8,c=4, hence c1=c2=c12=4 and rho=4. For EACH of H_1,H_2, (5) gives13/6 versus the best independent bound2, a strict gain1/6. For H_3 both give2. All conclusions use the SAME deterministic gluing (13). The exact three-bit joint table is supplied by the accompanying rational polygon-clipping verifier.

For these specified caps the middle residual volume is6. The old all-status anchored root credit for relation1 is zero because

    (sqrt4+sqrt8)/2=1+sqrt2<sqrt6;

the relation2 root average is2<sqrt6, so its root credit is also zero. Thus this particular capwise improvement is not already supplied by those two residual-root credits. It remains a directional certificate: for a horizontal or vertical continuous cap the two events in (13) are nested or identical, so taking an infimum over all normals eliminates the strict crossing gain. No improved global depth is claimed for (11).

## 7. Exact failures of automatic gain and archived calibrations

**Coincident copies.** On the actual product chain {-1,0,1,2} times K, use the same relations (12) and the diagonal uniform coupling X_z=X for every source. Both target points equal X. Then A_(1,i)=A_(2,i) for EVERY ambient cap, all i, and (7) equals its old fixed-packing bound exactly. Arbitrary extra caps do not produce crossing. More generally actual image coincidences remain a genuine obstruction even when marginals have sharp density ceilings.

**The (1/4,1,1) residual-credit example.** Its base has only three points -1,0,1. At the middle base there is exactly one nontrivial anchored representation by other bases, with coefficients1/2,1/2. Thus the hypothesis of two distinct relations sharing a source is absent. Adding the target itself as a source only creates a self-reference and is explicitly excluded in (1). This new lemma does not repair that example.

**The parity-forest coincident-copy example.** In `candidate d0f838592db846be`, use target p=(1,1), shared source s=(2,1), and relations

    p=[(2,1)+(0,1)]/2,
    p=[(2,1)+(1,2)+(0,0)]/3.

Their exclusive source sets are disjoint. The archived source centers are affine in the base. The large-square radii are1/10 and small-square radii1/100. Couple every square by the same uniform parameter in [-1,1]^2. Both target images are centered at the target center (3,-1), with radii11/200 and7/100 respectively, inside its radius1/10 fiber. Every cap in the archived twelve-cap menu is either strictly full or strictly empty on that entire target fiber. Therefore the two target signature vectors coincide for that WHOLE menu, and every gain in (7) is zero. This checks the actual geometric obstruction, not merely a formal possibility of overlapping marginal densities.

These examples show exactly what has and has not improved: shared-source adaptive credit retains a real intersection statistic and can strictly beat fixed independent allocation. There is no automatic lower bound for that crossing statistic from convex compatibility, volume, density ceilings, or a parity forest alone.
